stories.title: At least three wounded as earthquake rattles Peru
article_sentences: BUENOS AIRES, August 21.
At least three people were wounded in the 7.2-magnitude earthquake that shook Peru, Peru’s National Institute of Civil Defense (INDECI) said.
"The health ministry’s crisis response center informs that at this point, three patients received medical care at a hospital in Coracora," the authority said in a statement.
The RPP radio station said over 20 buildings were damaged.
According to the Geophysical Institute of Peru, a 7.2-magnitude earthquake struck 35 kilometers north of the Central Peruvian city of Coracora on Thursday, at the depth of 108 kilometers.

stories.title: Broken toilets, leaking roofs: Why India's 'cockroach' party wants to fix schools
stories.summary: The squat one-storey building has recently received a fresh coat of paint and looks respectable from a distance. But this government-run primary school for girls in Faridabad, a district on the outskirts of the Indian capital Delhi, suffers from a host of problems. The road outside the school in Khedi Kalan village is dotted with shallow potholes filled with filthy water. Inside, local social worker Satpal Narwat points out the plaster falling from the ceiling. "It looks new from the outside, but it's crumbling from inside. Four of its eight toilets are unusable and full of trash, while four of the nine classrooms have also been abandoned because they are too unsafe for children," he says, adding that in the rains, "the classrooms get flooded and children have no place to sit". This is not an isolated case. Many schools, especially in rural India, are starved of funding and in disrepair. India spends only 4.1% of its GDP on education. While this meets Unesco's lower minimum threshold of 4%, several countries - including France, Germany, Australia, Brazil and the US - spend more than 5% of their GDP on education. Countries like Belgium and Sweden spend even more. and the Indian government's own National Education Policy (NEP) - have recommended 6% as the ideal mark for India.

stories.title: Musk agrees that state debt of $50 trillion will be critical for US
stories.summary: Earlier this week, the US state debt exceeded record $40 trillion
article_sentences: NEW YORK, August 21.
US entrepreneur Elon Musk agreed with the opinion that things will start to fall apart for the United States when the state debt reaches the $50-trillion mark.
"Accurate graph," he wrote, commenting on a post of a user who posted a diagram designating the $50-trillion mark as the critical point.
Earlier this week, the US state debt exceeded record $40 trillion, increasing by $20 trillion in less than 10 years.
The International Monetary Fund (IMF) projects the US GDP growth to be at 2.3% in 2026.
